newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Sabena sees small 1997 loss, profit in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Sabena sees small 1997 loss, profit in 1998.

text.p: Belgian national airline Sabena on Thursday reiterated it aimed to narrow losses in 1997 and return to profit in 1998.
"Our 1997 budget still sees a loss, but a much smaller loss," Sabena Chairman Valere Croes told a news conference.
He said the 1997 budget was approved unanimously by its board, which includes representatives from dominant shareholder Swissair and the Belgian state, at a board meeting on Monday.
Croes said there would be an assessment of Sabena's financial situation after six months and that additional cost-cutting measures would be taken if needed.

Swissair has a 49.5 percent stake in Sabena, which had a 1995 group loss before provisions of 530 million Belgian francs ($15.7 million) and two billion franc ($59.2 million) net loss in the first half of 1996.
"Sabena has had a bad year," said Croes who declined to give a full-year 1996 forecast.
